en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a nearly perfect symmetrical cone that is clearly visible from Legazpi City.
The Cagayan River carries brown water due to eroded soil washed down from the Sierra Madre mountains.
Volcano Island sits inside Taal Lake in Batangas, where observers can often see steam rising from the water.
Mount Pulag in Benguet is frequently covered in a thick sea of clouds that hikers walk above.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features visible stalactites and stalagmites formed by dripping mineral-rich water.
The famous white sand of Boracay Island in Aklan is made of finely crushed coral and shells.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season because the grass covering them dries up.
Maria Cristina Falls in Lanao del Norte plunges down a high cliff, creating a constant, visible mist below.
The roots of mangrove trees in the Olango Island wildlife sanctuary are visibly tangled above the muddy tidal water.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao look like giant green stairs carved directly into the mountains.
The Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur features visibly clear, bright blue water flowing from a deep underwater cave.
The Tubbataha Reefs in the Sulu Sea feature visible coral atolls that form a ring around a deep lagoon.
